title: WARC World Model Learns 56 ARC-AGI-3 Mechanics in 80 Steps
summary: Third Intelligence's 35M-parameter WARC vision transformer masters 56 of 69 ARC-AGI-3 mechanics through test-time training, tripling benchmark scores.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Third Intelligence's WARC vision transformer reaches 80% accuracy on 56 of 69 ARC-AGI-3 mechanics in approximately 80 exposures each.
- The 35M-parameter model updates all weights after every game transition, achieving 69.1% mechanic accuracy versus 24.7% for DreamerV3 baselines.
- Paired with a graph explorer, WARC-Agent triples efficiency scores from 0.15 to 0.46 on public games and scores 0.20 on Kaggle's hidden leaderboard.


Third Intelligence has released WARC, a 35-million-parameter vision transformer that rewrites all of its weights during live gameplay to master abstract reasoning tasks. Officially released on November 10, 2026, the model reaches 80% prediction accuracy on 56 of 69 game mechanics catalogued in the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, with half of those mechanics crossing the threshold in roughly 80 observations. The research paper, authored by Haruto Kawano, Shota Takashiro, and Kohei Hayashi from Third Intelligence and the University of Tokyo, demonstrates that aggressive test-time training on a small model can outperform much larger frozen baselines on reasoning benchmarks.


## How WARC Updates Weights in Real Time


WARC's architecture is a 35M-parameter vision transformer that performs full-parameter test-time training after every valid transition in a game. The model executes 20 gradient steps following each observation, continuously rewriting its weights as it encounters new mechanics. This approach contrasts sharply with traditional frozen models: when WARC's weights are locked during testing, mechanic accuracy collapses to 18.4%, with the paper noting that "without updates only one in seven does at all." The model first pretrains on gameplay from other grid-world games before adapting to each new ARC-AGI-3 challenge through this rapid weight-update loop.


The MechEval benchmark labels 69 recurring mechanics across 20 public ARC-AGI-3 games, providing a granular test of how quickly a[world model](https://emergent.sh/glossary/world-model) internalizes specific game rules. WARC achieves 69.1% mechanic accuracy across all exposures, substantially ahead of a 50M-parameter DreamerV3 baseline at 30.1% and an episodic-retrieval baseline at 32.9%. The test-time training budget is not trivial: each action consumes roughly 0.74 seconds on an RTX PRO 6000 GPU, accumulating to 8.6 hours for a full Kaggle submission.


## Benchmark Performance and Efficiency Scores


When paired with a fixed graph explorer that hashes game states and selects actions predicted to produce maximally novel frames, WARC-Agent triples the explorer's official efficiency score from 0.15 to 0.46 on the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games. The paper attributes most of this gain to test-time training rather than improved exploration heuristics. On the Kaggle hidden-game leaderboard, the system scores 0.20, well below the 1.39 Oracle ceiling reported in the paper but demonstrating generalization to unseen mechanics. The closed-loop RHAE score jumps from 0.15 to 0.46, reflecting the model's ability to leverage learned dynamics for more effective exploration.


## Ablation Studies Isolate Key Design Choices


Ablation experiments isolate the contributions of pretraining and update frequency. Removing pretraining on other games drops mechanic accuracy by 34.1 percentage points, confirming that transfer from related tasks is essential for rapid adaptation. Updating weights every five transitions instead of every single transition costs 10.5 points, showing that the aggressive update schedule is not merely a marginal optimization. The paper does not explore intermediate update frequencies or adaptive schedules, leaving room for follow-on work to balance compute cost against learning speed.


## What This Means


WARC demonstrates that small vision transformers with aggressive test-time training can master abstract reasoning mechanics faster than larger frozen models, shifting the efficiency frontier for interactive world models. The 35M-parameter count and per-transition update loop make WARC a practical candidate for embodied agents that must adapt to novel environments with limited compute budgets. By publishing both the model and the MechEval benchmark, Third Intelligence provides a reproducible testbed for future research into adaptive world models. The gap between the 0.20 Kaggle score and the 1.39 Oracle ceiling signals that exploration strategies and mechanic generalization remain open challenges for the next generation of interactive reasoning systems.
